# <a id="_8tpyzs6mqo2a"></a>__The Thanksgiving Turkey’s Tactical Strike__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 19, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

In our family, pranks aren’t just jokes; they are coordinated maneuvers\. My nephew, a boy who once survived trying to “Superboy” his way across a river and jumping onto subway lines, had reached high school age but hadn’t lost his appetite for mischief\. My husband, usually my partner in all things, was his secret ally in a long\-running “Ice Cube War\.”

The setting was a dignified Thanksgiving dinner hosted by my sister’s church at the local Community Center\. To add to the festive spirit, the church put on a little show, and my nephew was cast in the starring role: he was dressed in a full, feathered, glorious turkey costume\.

I committed the ultimate tactical error: I sat with my back to the stage\. My husband, however, sat with his back to the wall, giving him a panoramic view of the entire room\. He was perfectly positioned to see the “turkey” descend from the stage and begin a slow, silent stalk across the Community Center floor\.

Unbeknownst to me, my sister’s pastor was sitting at the very next table\.

My husband didn’t say a word\. He didn’t blink\. He didn’t even give me the “look” that says something is amiss\. He watched that giant turkey sneak closer and closer with the poker face of a high\-stakes pinochle player\. When the turkey reached me, he didn’t gobble; he reached down and dumped a handful of ice cubes directly down the back of my shirt\.

The shock was so cold and so sudden that my filter vanished\. A cuss word—not the “F\-word,” mind you, but a distinct, loud cuss word—flew out of my mouth before I could catch it\. It rang out across the quiet dinner, reaching the ears of every parishioner nearby, including the pastor\.

For years afterward, every time I visited that church, I felt the pastor’s eyes on me\. I wasn’t just “the sister”; I was “The Lady Who Cussed at the Thanksgiving Dinner\.” It took a whole new pastor being hired for me to finally feel like my criminal record had been cleared\. My nephew got his laugh, and my husband—the skunk—got away with the perfect distraction\.
